reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it explains an IBM Technical Support Associate recruitment opportunity and how eligible viewers can apply. The demonstrated process involves signing in and completing an application form, and the speaker states that no application fee is required. The material does not establish that the external recruitment site is safe or that the application led to hiring, but it presents the content as job-application guidance rather than an investment or financial-return offer.

opening.argument: The video links a viewer action to an attractive employment opportunity: it presents an IBM recruitment offer for multiple graduation batches and instructs viewers to create an account, provide personal and educational information, upload a resume, and submit an application. The speaker also emphasizes that applying is free. That combination functions as a low-friction solicitation for participation and personal data, even though the material does not prove fraudulent hiring. The evidence does not independently establish that the advertised opportunity will produce employment or any other benefit.

A free application can still be a deceptive participation funnel; absence of a fee does not resolve that concern.

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals appear together: the description directs viewers to a Telegram channel and an application URL, while the instructions lead through sign-in and collection of names, addresses, phone numbers, education, and a resume. The video also tells viewers to continue through a submission process and predicts an application-complete outcome. That combination creates a plausible concern that viewers are being moved from promotional content into external account and data-collection flows. It does not prove deception, but the available evidence does not rule out misuse of the linked process or submitted information.
